holidays.name: National Cheese Doodle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the crunchy, puffy, orange-fingered snack that leaves a telltale dusting on keyboards, couches, and shirts everywhere. Fans are encouraged to snack proudly and embrace the mess.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it was created by snack fans and food-holiday calendars rather than by any official proclamation, and it has been observed on March 5 for years.
holidays.funFact: Cheese puffs became popular in the 1930s after the Flakall Corporation of Wisconsin figured out that corn meal extruded through a machine would puff up, leading to the first mass-produced cheese puffs, Korn Kurls.

holidays.name: National Absinthe Day
holidays.description: A day for raising a glass to the famously mysterious green spirit once nicknamed 'the Green Fairy,' enjoyed traditionally by slowly dripping ice-cold water over a sugar cube.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the March 5, 2007 repeal of the long-standing US ban on absinthe, after it had been prohibited since 1912.
holidays.funFact: Absinthe was blamed for madness and moral decay in the early 1900s, but modern science says the supposed hallucinations were most likely caused by its very high alcohol content and by cheap, adulterated versions, not by the wormwood.

holidays.name: Multiple Personality Day
holidays.description: A day of awareness about dissociative identity disorder, which has often been misrepresented in movies and pop culture. It encourages learning the facts and replacing myths with understanding and compassion.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial awareness observance listed on March 5 in many holiday calendars, intended to encourage education and empathy around dissociative disorders.
holidays.funFact: The condition is now formally called dissociative identity disorder, and experts note that it is far more often portrayed as dramatic in fiction than it appears in real life.
